intended_object: An isomorphism of topological H-representations Res^G_H C(G,B) ≅ C(H, C(G/H, B)), for a profinite group G (compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected), a closed subgroup H and a topological G-representation B. Both sides carry the twisted coinduced action and H acts pointwise on C(G/H, B). This is the restriction clause of NSW Prop. 1.3.6(ii): a coinduced G-module is H-coinduced. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the general lemma it specializes.
explanation:
The definition plugs the profinite library's continuous coset section `H.continuousCosetRepresentative` into the library's general `coind₁RestrictionIso`, which works for any topological group with a chosen continuous section of G → G/H. It also uses that a closed subgroup of a compact group is compact.

I checked the general construction by hand:
- The map t ↦ (t·s(t⁻¹H), t⁻¹H) is a homeomorphism G ≅ H × G/H.
- The forward map F(h)(c) = f(h·s(c)⁻¹) is H-equivariant. Indeed, (h₀·f)(h s(c)⁻¹) = ρ(h₀) f(h₀⁻¹ h s(c)⁻¹), and this is the coind₁ action of h₀ on F followed by the pointwise action on C(G/H, B).
- Currying and uncurrying give continuous linear maps between the compact-open spaces.

So this is the intended isomorphism, non-canonical because it depends on the chosen section, as the docstring says.

Generality: profinite groups with closed subgroups are exactly the setting of NSW Prop. 1.3.6(ii). There the continuous section exists automatically, and providing it is the whole content of this specialization. The fully general version, with an arbitrary topological group and a chosen continuous section, already exists in the library itself, so this definition is not too narrow. The coefficient ring may be any topological ring, which is as general as Mathlib's `TopRep`. Mathlib has `coind₁`, `res` and the comparison map `coind₁Res`, but not this isomorphism.
